read_scope.notes: Read all extracted text on pages 1–22, including references and Appendices A–G; visually inspected rendered versions of every page and all six figures and eight tables. Consulted the frozen paper.tex, specificity_results.tex, specificity_model_table.tex, and specificity_review_table.tex to resolve notation, table presentation, and source locations. The abstract has 155 whitespace-delimited words in the supplied source. No other review, prior assessment, working-tree manuscript, or progress record was consulted.

score_reasons.expression: The English is fluent, precise, and generally economical at sentence level. The opening Monet–Sisley example immediately establishes a useful distinction; Sections 3.2–3.3 state the experimental arms and measurement units clearly. Recurrent qualifications accumulate across Sections 4–6 and figure captions, however, and technical noun phrases such as “labeled, centered mean configuration” and “global cross-repeat-corrected named/free squared change” make some central statements harder to absorb than necessary. This is strong writing with material opportunities to improve pace, rather than prose requiring wholesale repair.
score_reasons.structure: The manuscript has a coherent question–design–measurement–results progression, clearly labels post-result analyses, and places exact feature definitions and historical cohorts in optional appendices. The hierarchy weakens within the results: the common response that leads the abstract appears only in Section 5.4, after substantial retrospective diagnostics; that subsection also ends with a paragraph about primary-error robustness rather than common shifts or distributional proximity. Tables 2 and 3 do not visually foreground the comparisons around which the narrative is organized.
score_reasons.new_reader_understanding: A new reader can recover the study, the six prompt conditions, the collection-relative target, and the major conclusions without the repository. Table 1, the D=0 and D=1 interpretations, the 0/r/2r example, and explicit distinctions between point estimates and tests are valuable. Section 4 nevertheless starts with densely indexed vectors before a concrete explanation of what centering and projection retain; some of the best intuition comes after the equations. Table 3 is dominated by symbols, Figure 2 lacks a worked reading cue, and the standalone abstract does not identify the calibration as a retrospective feature-vector counterfactual.
score_reasons.engagement: The question is consequential and specific, and the same-scene image grid and artist-pair heatmap reward inspection. The findings about uneven painter distinctions and the reversal after calibration create a discernible narrative without hype. Momentum diminishes through the long sequence of metrics, numerical diagnostics, and repeated exclusions of interpretations. The main figures receive little affirmative explanation of what the reader should notice, and the common-effect result is delayed despite its prominence in the title and abstract.

strengths: The first introduction paragraph uses Monet and Sisley to explain why proximity to a painter collection does not establish correct differences between painter labels.

Sections 3.1–3.3 clearly distinguish the primary reference panel from the development scaler, explain equal painter weighting, state the six prompt conditions and the 1,008-image design, and explain what a standardized feature unit means.
The D=0/D=1 benchmarks, finite-negative-estimate explanation, and scene-wise versus aggregate decomposition give readers meaningful ways to interpret an otherwise unfamiliar endpoint.

The manuscript consistently distinguishes declared inference from retrospective diagnostics, point orderings from supported pairwise comparisons, and digital reference agreement from perceptual artistic fidelity.
Figure 1 uses a systematic same-brief comparison across all six models; Figure 3 includes every artist pair and numerical cell labels rather than highlighting only favorable contrasts.

The discussion and conclusion retain the weakened Sunburst comparison after source correction, and Appendix F retains the contrary prospective transfer result. These details support a bounded, credible narrative.
The PDF is cleanly typeset without observed clipping or overlapping content, remains 22 pages, and the supplied abstract stays at the 155-word limit.

findings.issue: The main measurement narrative opens with mu, r, H, and a four-index generated vector, then introduces projection and two error decompositions before giving its simplest example. For the specified audience, “one vectorized reference configuration” remains an abstract object despite the correct definitions. The regression equation also repeats a comparison already explained in paired-scene terms.
findings.reader_effect: Readers must learn the notation while reconstructing the conceptual operation, increasing the chance that they treat beta as an ordinary similarity score or D as a generic style distance. This interrupts the transition from the very concrete design to the results.
findings.suggested_change: Move and rewrite the existing 0/r/2r example to precede the derivations: no painter differences give expected D=1; matching the reference differences gives D=0; doubling those differences returns D to 1. Precede Equation 1 with a brief statement that each painter is represented by how its measurements differ from the four-painter average, and that beta counts the component pointing along the reference differences while D also counts the remaining mismatch. Retain Equations 1–3 and the scene-target interpretation; move the redundant fixed-effects equation to Appendix B, and consider placing the secondary energy formula in Appendix C. Use the recovered space for intuition rather than adding pages.

findings.location: Section 5.1 and Table 2, pp. 7–8; Section 5.3 and Table 3, pp. 9–10
findings.issue: The main comparison table displays only contrasts against GPT Image 2, all of whose intervals include zero, while the two resolved comparisons highlighted in the prose are against FLUX. Table 3 then presents the ranking reversal using five mostly symbolic headers and omits the primary uncalibrated D, requiring readers to look back to Table 2.
findings.reader_effect: The tables make it unnecessarily difficult to verify the central inferential result and the before/after calibration comparison. A reader scanning the principal table can miss the supported differences altogether.
findings.suggested_change: Present the already-computed FLUX-referenced contrasts in Table 2, explicitly retaining the same fixed 21-comparison family and the full 15-pair table in Appendix E. Add the existing primary D column beside Dheld in Table 3 and use short plain-language header labels alongside the symbols, such as pooled error, scene variation, contrast power, alignment, and calibrated error. Group the decomposition columns separately from the calibration columns. These are display changes using existing results, not new tests.

findings.location: Section 5, particularly Sections 5.3–5.5, pp. 9–11; specificity_results.tex lines 86–151
findings.issue: The common-response result that leads the abstract is deferred until Section 5.4, after the reader has processed artist omissions, calibration, content targets, and genuine-painting controls. Section 5.4 also ends with primary-error weighting and texture sensitivities that do not fit its common-shift/distributional-proximity heading.
findings.reader_effect: The central question loses prominence, and readers have to maintain several diagnostic threads before reaching the evidence for the title’s shared-effect framing. The last paragraph of Section 5.4 feels like a return to an earlier argument.
findings.suggested_change: Bring a concise common-response finding forward immediately after the primary contrast result, then progress to uneven artist pairs and calibration. Keep the distributional-energy detail secondary. Move the primary-error robustness paragraph into a compact robustness subsection with source correction; reduce the genuine-painting-control paragraph to its interpretive result and point to Appendix C.1 for the two-draw and exact-mean ranges. Preserve the distinction between declared and post-result analyses while reorganizing by the question each answers.

findings.issue: The abstract places the painter-pair and calibration findings alongside the primary findings without marking their retrospective status. “Scaling measured contrasts using other scenes changes which model has the lowest estimated error” also leaves a standalone reader to infer whether the scaling was applied to images, to a generation procedure, or only to measured feature vectors.
findings.reader_effect: A reader who sees only the abstract can overestimate the evidential status or practical realizability of the calibration result, even though Sections 4.5 and 5.3 make the limits clear.
findings.suggested_change: Replace the calibration sentence with a concise explicit formulation such as “Post-result scalar calibration of feature contrasts changes the model with lowest estimated error.” Identify the artist-pair analysis as descriptive if space permits. Recover any words by shortening the sample-description or final qualification sentences; do not exceed the present 155-word abstract.

findings.location: Figure 2 and its lead-in/caption, p. 8; Figure 1, p. 4
findings.issue: Figure 2 supplies a correct legend and projection caveats, but the main text says only that it illustrates the contrasts. It does not show a new reader how to read the displacement between a same-colored generated mean and reference cross, how the origin relates to centering, or why dispersed points can coexist with a near-unit aggregate slope. Figure 1 similarly supplies provenance rather than a short reading guide.
findings.reader_effect: The figures are attractive but do less explanatory work than their space allows. Readers may inspect the paintings for perceived resemblance or the scatter panels for cluster separation without connecting either display to the measured target.
findings.suggested_change: Replace part of Figure 2’s generic caution with a concrete reading instruction: compare each colored circle with its same-colored cross; the origin is the four-painter average, and remaining separation is disagreement in the displayed reference axes. Add a brief textual walkthrough connecting one visible panel to an already-reported numerical result, while retaining the 31-coordinate/projection limitation. For Figure 1, direct attention to changes across painter clauses within each model row and repeat the short river brief in the main-text lead-in if space can be recovered from provenance details already in Appendix D.

findings.location: Introduction; Sections 4–6 and repeated figure-caption qualifications, pp. 1, 5–11
findings.issue: The qualifications are mostly justified, but the paper repeatedly restates broad limitations already established: the target is not validated artistic style, positive alignment is not full recovery, and the results do not establish perceptual confusion or fidelity. Dense clusters of such sentences sometimes follow an informative result with several exclusions before the next positive interpretation.
findings.reader_effect: Readers repeatedly revisit the boundary of the claim instead of learning what the result reveals, slowing an otherwise coherent empirical narrative.
findings.suggested_change: Keep the collection-relative boundary in the introduction and limitations, and keep unique local warnings where they prevent a specific misreading, such as negative D, scene variation, or non-realizable calibration. Cut duplicate general artistic-fidelity disclaimers from intervening captions and paragraphs, and use some of that space for short affirmative interpretations of the numerical results. In Section 5.4, for example, state that most measured named/free change is shared and the generic clause reproduces part of its direction, then give the technical covariance correction in the appendix.

findings.location: Data and code availability, p. 12; paper.tex line 455
findings.issue: “Appendix D displays 36 generated and four reference examples” is an inaccurate locator. Appendix D displays Figure 4’s 12 generated controls; the other 24 generated examples and four reference paintings are in Figure 1 in the main text.
findings.reader_effect: A reader seeking the advertised complete image set in Appendix D may think examples are missing.
findings.suggested_change: Replace the sentence with “Figures 1 and 4 display 36 generated and four reference examples; Appendix D documents their selection and identities.” Distinguish displayed identities from byte hashes retained in the manifest.

claim_fidelity_issues: The abstract’s calibration sentence does not identify the operation as a retrospective feature-vector counterfactual; the full paper does. This is a localized standalone-abstract ambiguity, not evidence that the main results claim an implemented image improvement.
The data-availability statement attributes all 36 generated and four reference examples to Appendix D, although the examples are split between main-text Figure 1 and Appendix Figure 4.
summary: A careful and coherent bounded empirical audit, with strong English and unusually explicit distinctions among response, alignment, uncertainty, and artistic fidelity. The main remaining editorial work is to lower the initial conceptual burden of the metrics, make the central comparisons immediately visible, and tighten the result sequence and repeated qualifications. These changes can be made by moving and replacing material within the existing 22 pages; no new experiment, feature representation, or perceptual study is needed.
